method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.coverageNote: Diagnosis frameworks and first-line systemic therapy are both in the review. A short 'guide to diagnosis' PMC record contained only an abstract and was not used.

mcqs.question: Which diagnostic aids does the review cite?

options.A: An international Delphi consensus, and the PARACELSUS score aimed especially at distinguishing venous leg ulcers
options.B: A mandatory skin culture that proves the diagnosis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: An international Delphi consensus, and the PARACELSUS score aimed especially at distinguishing venous leg ulcers
mcqs.explanation: Diagnosis is supported by an international expert Delphi consensus, and PARACELSUS was proposed particularly for the differential diagnosis with venous leg ulcers.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Another set of criteria, the PARACELSUS score, has been proposed by a German group, particularly for the differential diagnosis with venous leg ulcers

mcqs.question: In STOP GAP, which regimens were compared?

options.A: Oral prednisolone 0.75 mg/kg/day versus cyclosporine 4 mg/kg/day

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Oral prednisolone 0.75 mg/kg/day versus cyclosporine 4 mg/kg/day
mcqs.explanation: Patients received oral prednisolone 0.75 mg/kg/day or cyclosporine 4 mg/kg/day.

sourceRefs.excerpt: patients either received oral prednisolone 0.75 mg/kg/day or cyclosporine 4 mg/kg/day.

mcqs.question: What was the primary comparative result of STOP GAP as stated here?

options.A: No difference in speed of healing over 6 weeks or in the other listed clinical outcomes
options.B: Cyclosporine healed ulcers twice as fast
options.D: Both drugs healed every ulcer by 6 weeks
options.E: The trial was stopped for excess mortality with prednisolone

mcqs.correctAnswerText: No difference in speed of healing over 6 weeks or in the other listed clinical outcomes
mcqs.explanation: There was no difference in speed of healing over 6 weeks, time to healing, response, inflammation, pain, quality of life, failures, or time to recurrence.

sourceRefs.excerpt: There was no difference between the two treatments in terms of speed of healing over 6 weeks, time to healing, treatment response, inflammation resolution, pain, quality of life, treatment failures, and time to recurrence.

mcqs.question: What longer-term healing and recurrence figures does the review give for STOP GAP?

options.A: Almost half unhealed at 6 months, and almost a third recurred, median 582 days in both groups
options.B: All ulcers healed by 6 weeks with no recurrence
options.C: Recurrence only in the cyclosporine arm at 30 days

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Almost half unhealed at 6 months, and almost a third recurred, median 582 days in both groups
mcqs.explanation: Almost half on systemic corticosteroid or cyclosporine had unhealed ulcers at 6 months, and almost a third recurred, with median time to recurrence 582 days in both groups.

sourceRefs.excerpt: almost half of the enrolled patients receiving systemic CS or cyclosporine did not obtain healing of PG ulcers at 6 months, and almost a third of patients in both treatment groups developed a disease recurrence, with a median time to recurrence of 582 days in both groups.

mcqs.question: What pulse-corticosteroid regimen is described?

options.A: Intravenous methylprednisolone 1000 mg for 3–5 consecutive days, then oral corticosteroid
options.D: Intramuscular triamcinolone every week for a year
options.E: Pulse steroids are said to be contraindicated

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Intravenous methylprednisolone 1000 mg for 3–5 consecutive days, then oral corticosteroid
mcqs.explanation: Pulse therapy with 1000 mg intravenous methylprednisolone for 3–5 consecutive days, followed by oral corticosteroid, may act faster and help taper the oral drug.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Pulse therapy with 1000 mg of intravenous methylprednisolone for 3–5 consecutive days, followed by oral CS, may have a faster onset of action and may also help taper oral CS
